import html # Pre‑existing HTML template. # The placeholders {writer_name}, {title}, {body} and {tags} # will be replaced by the escaped values below. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

Posted by: {writer_name}

{body}
{tags}
""" def generate_post_html(writer_name: str, title: str, body: str, tag_list: list[str]) -> str: """ Build a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- writer_name : str Name of the author. title : str Post headline. body : str Main text of the post. tag_list : list[str] Tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str XSS‑protected HTML string. """ # Basic type checks – raise informative errors if types are wrong if not isinstance(writer_name, str): raise TypeError("writer_name must be a string") if not isinstance(title, str): raise TypeError("title must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise TypeError("body must be a string") if not (isinstance(tag_list, list) and all(isinstance(t, str) for t in tag_list)): raise TypeError("tag_list must be a list of strings") # Escape user supplied text to avoid XSS esc_writer = html.escape(writer_name, quote=True) esc_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) esc_body = html.escape(body) # Wrap each tag in a element, escaping the tag text itself escaped_tags = " ".join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in tag_list ) # Populate the template with escaped values html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( writer_name=esc_writer, title=esc_title, body=esc_body, tags=escaped_tags ) return html_output.strip()
